context.title: Lord of the Sabbath
context.summary: Conflicts over the Sabbath lead the Pharisees to plot against Jesus. He withdraws, is accused of casting out demons by Beelzebub, warns against blasphemy of the Spirit, offers only the sign of Jonah, and redefines his family.
context.background: The law let a hungry traveler pick grain by hand from a neighbor's field (Deuteronomy 23:25). The dispute was about the Sabbath: Pharisees counted plucking grain as harvesting work. Jesus answers from Scripture.

customs.note: Twelve loaves set out each Sabbath before God, later eaten only by priests (Leviticus 24:5-9).
A name for the prince of demons, probably related to Baal-zebub, a Philistine god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2).

watchFor: Matthew's longest Old Testament quotation, from Isaiah's servant song (vv. 18–21).
'One greater than the temple' (v. 6), 'a greater than Jonas' (v. 41), 'a greater than Solomon' (v. 42).
Family is defined by doing the Father's will (v. 50).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Satan
people.summary: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7).

people.name: Jonah
people.summary: A dove, the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher. He was a prophet of Israel, and predicted the restoration of the ancient boundaries (2 Kings 14:25-27) of the kingdom.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

places.name: Nineveh
places.summary: First mentioned in Gen. 10:11, which is rendered in the Revised Version, “He [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria and builded Nineveh.” It is not again noticed till the days of Jonah, when it is described (Jonah 3:3; 4:11) as a great and populous city, the flourishing capital of the Assyrian empire (2 Kings 19:36; Isa. 37:37).
